items.followUp: Differentiate between a co-enzyme and an enzyme.

rubric.why: A prosthetic group is distinguished by being firmly attached to its enzyme.
rubric.description: States that a prosthetic group is tightly or permanently bound to an enzyme.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the tight or permanent attachment.

rubric.why: A co-enzyme associates less firmly with an enzyme than a prosthetic group does.
rubric.description: States that a co-enzyme is loosely or temporarily bound to an enzyme.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the loose or temporary association.

modelAnswer: A prosthetic group is tightly bound to its enzyme.
A co-enzyme is loosely bound to its enzyme and can dissociate readily.

items.followUp: Name the nitrogenous base, sugar and phosphate groups present in ATP.

rubric.why: Adenine and ribose are the base and sugar parts of ATP.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when both the base and sugar are identified.

rubric.description: States that ATP has three phosphate groups.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the three phosphate groups.

modelAnswer: ATP consists of adenine, ribose sugar and three phosphate groups.

items.followUp: State the main products of photosynthesis and respiration.

rubric.why: Photosynthesis uses light energy to make glucose from simple substances.
rubric.description: Explains that photosynthesis makes glucose using light energy, or identifies its use of carbon dioxide and water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the defining process of photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Respiration breaks down glucose and releases energy.
rubric.description: Explains that respiration breaks down glucose and releases energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the defining process of respiration.

modelAnswer: In photosynthesis, plants use light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water, releasing oxygen.
In respiration, glucose is broken down to release energy; oxygen is used and carbon dioxide and water are produced.

items.followUp: What is the role of iron in plants?

rubric.why: Magnesium is a key part of the chlorophyll molecule.
rubric.description: Identifies magnesium as a central atom or component of chlorophyll.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking magnesium with chlorophyll as a constituent.

rubric.why: Chlorophyll is required for photosynthesis, so magnesium supports this process.
rubric.description: Links magnesium or chlorophyll with photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating its role in photosynthesis.

modelAnswer: Magnesium is the central component of the chlorophyll molecule.
It is therefore essential for photosynthesis.

items.followUp: Differentiate between saturated and unsaturated fats.

rubric.why: Saturated fatty acids have no carbon-carbon double bonds.
rubric.description: States that saturated fatty acids have no double bonds between carbon atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct feature of saturated fatty acids.

rubric.why: Unsaturated fatty acids have one or more carbon-carbon double bonds.
rubric.description: States that unsaturated fatty acids have one or more double bonds between carbon atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct feature of unsaturated fatty acids.

modelAnswer: Saturated fatty acids have no double bonds between their carbon atoms.
Unsaturated fatty acids have one or more double bonds between their carbon atoms.

items.followUp: Explain how high humidity affects the rate of transpiration.

rubric.why: Moving air generally increases the rate of water loss from leaves.
rubric.description: States that wind increases the rate of transpiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct effect on the rate.

rubric.why: Wind carries away moist air near the leaf, maintaining a gradient for water vapour to diffuse out.
rubric.description: Explains that wind removes moist air or water vapour near the leaf, maintaining the diffusion gradient.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid explanation of the effect.

modelAnswer: Wind increases the rate of transpiration.
It carries away the humid air around the leaves, maintaining a diffusion gradient for water vapour to move out.

items.followUp: Name the parts of blood and state one function of any two of them.

rubric.why: Blood is classified as a fluid connective tissue.
rubric.description: Defines blood as a fluid connective tissue.

rubric.why: Blood has plasma and three types of formed elements: red cells, white cells and platelets.
rubric.description: Names plasma, red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming all four parts.

modelAnswer: Blood is a fluid connective tissue that circulates through the body.
Its parts are plasma, red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets.

items.followUp: Trace the route of blood in pulmonary circulation and systemic circulation.

rubric.why: Pulmonary circulation carries blood from the heart to the lungs and back to the heart.
rubric.description: Gives the pulmonary route: right ventricle to lungs to left atrium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct pulmonary route.

rubric.why: Systemic circulation carries blood from the heart to the body and back to the heart.
rubric.description: Gives the systemic route: left ventricle to the body to right atrium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct systemic route.

modelAnswer: Pulmonary circulation: blood flows from the right ventricle to the lungs and returns to the left atrium.
Systemic circulation: blood flows from the left ventricle to the body and returns to the right atrium.
